title: Machine learning identifies sediment-derived granites in the Hadean zircon record, supporting early subduction
summary: A machine-learning classifier trained on trace-element fingerprints identified detrital zircon signatures from sediment-derived S-type granites as old as 4.24 billion years in the Jack Hills record. Across global detrital zircon data, the authors report long-term cyclic changes in S-type granite proportions and infer that exposed, weathered continental crust and subduction operated by about 4.2 Ga. The result bears on early Earth geodynamics, not a direct fossil or biological discovery.
organization: Chinese Academy of Sciences; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences; Macau University of Science and Technology; University of California, Davis; Queen’s University

evidence.tested: A machine-learning classifier trained on trace-element fingerprints identified detrital zircon signatures from sediment-derived S-type granites as old as 4.24 billion years in the Jack Hills record.
evidence.unknown: The early-subduction interpretation is inferred from zircon trace elements and remains one interpretation of sparse Hadean geological evidence. The article reports that only the combination of early subaerial weathering and subduction explains the prevalence of the inferred S-type granites; it does not directly observe tectonics at 4.2 Ga.
evidence.ai_role: Classified zircon as S-type or non-S-type from multielement geochemical fingerprints, allowing the authors to identify the oldest sediment-derived granite signal and quantify its temporal distribution across detrital-zircon records.
